ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in quadrilateral $ABCD$, $AD\parallel BC\parallel EF$. If $AE=3$, $AB=8$, $CD=10$, then what is the length of $CF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\[
\textbf{Solution:} \quad \text{Since } AD\parallel BC\parallel EF, 
\]
\[
\therefore \frac{AE}{AB}=\frac{DF}{CD},
\]
\[
\text{Since } AE=3, AB=8, CD=10,
\]
\[
\therefore \frac{3}{8}=\frac{DF}{10},
\]
\[
\text{Solving for } DF, \text{ we get } DF=\frac{15}{4},
\]
\[
\therefore CF=CD-DF=10-\frac{15}{4}=\boxed{\frac{25}{4}}.
\]

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the attached figure, quadrilateral ABCD is in the shape of a trapezoid, AD is the upper horizontal side, BC is the lower horizontal side, and AB and CD are the left and right two slanted sides respectively; point E is on AB, point F is on CD, and EF is an internal horizontal line, parallel to AD and BC. Then reason: Given AE=3 and AB=8, so EB=AB-AE=8-3=5. Since AD∥EF∥BC, these three parallel lines intersect the two slanted sides AB and CD. According to the intercept theorem, AE/EB=DF/FC. Solve the ratio split of CD into parts 3:5, giving FC = 5/(3+5) · 10 = 25/4.
